description: Vocabulaire de la paix (peacekeeping, peacemaking…) et du changement (transform, amend, revert, reverse, reform…).

questions.question: What is the difference between peacekeeping and peacemaking?
choix: peacemaking = negotiating an end to a conflict; peacekeeping = maintaining a ceasefire on the ground
they mean exactly the same thing
peacemaking is only economic aid
peacekeeping = negotiating; peacemaking = sending soldiers
questions.explication: Peacemaking = rétablir la paix par la négociation ; peacekeeping = la maintenir sur le terrain (Casques bleus) ; peacebuilding = la consolider.

questions.question: The UN was created to maintain international ___ and security.
All member states have one ___ in the General Assembly.
The Security Council can authorize ___ action against an aggressor. (indice : militaire)
The Security Council can authorize ___ missions to keep the peace.
The UN promotes human ___ and sustainable development.
The Secretary-General represents the ___ as a whole. (indice : l'Organisation)
Which of these are usually considered SUCCESSES of the UN? (plusieurs réponses)
choix: Efficiency and bureaucracy
Human Rights Protection (setting global standards)
Humanitarian Aid
Health and Development
Ability to prevent major wars and genocides
Equal representation in the Security Council
questions.explication: C'est débattu, mais l'aide humanitaire, la santé (ex. éradication de la variole) et la définition des droits de l'homme sont souvent vus comme des réussites ; la bureaucratie, la représentation inégale (P5) et l'échec face à Rwanda/Srebrenica comme des échecs.

questions.question: Which of these are usually considered FAILURES or weaknesses of the UN? (plusieurs réponses)
choix: Ability to prevent major wars and genocides
Efficiency and bureaucracy
Health and Development
Humanitarian Aid
Equal representation
questions.explication: Lourdeur bureaucratique, P5 non représentatifs, génocides du Rwanda (1994) et de Srebrenica (1995)…

questions.question: What needs adapting to make the UN more efficient? (idées)
questions.verso: Reform the Security Council (more permanent seats for Africa, Latin America, limit the veto) · cut bureaucracy and duplication (cf. UN80) · secure stable funding · give the General Assembly more weight · make peacekeeping mandates more robust.

questions.question: transform sth
questions.verso: transformer — completely change the appearance or character of sth, often to make it better. Ex : Computers have transformed our lives. Nom : transformation.

questions.question: What does « transform sth » mean?
choix: a process or period of change from one state to another
make changes to correct a mistake or improve a law, statement, document
completely change the appearance or character of sth, often to make it better
change sth so it is the opposite of what it was before (reverse a decision/trend/policy)
questions.explication: transform sth = transformer. Ex : Computers have transformed our lives.

questions.question: amend sth
questions.verso: amender, modifier — make changes to correct a mistake or improve a law, statement, document. Ex : Civil servants are now amending the document. Nom : amendment.

questions.question: What does « amend sth » mean?
choix: completely change the appearance or character of sth, often to make it better
make changes to correct a mistake or improve a law, statement, document
learn and get used to sth which is new and different
change your behaviour in order to be more successful in a new situation (syn. adjust to)
questions.explication: amend sth = amender, modifier. Ex : Civil servants are now amending the document.

questions.question: adapt to sth
questions.verso: s'adapter à — change your behaviour in order to be more successful in a new situation (syn. adjust to). Ex : We must adapt to a changing world. Nom : adaptation.

questions.question: What does « adapt to sth » mean?
choix: change gradually, often from something simple to something more complicated
completely change the appearance or character of sth, often to make it better
improve a system, an organization, a law by making changes to it
change your behaviour in order to be more successful in a new situation (syn. adjust to)
questions.explication: adapt to sth = s'adapter à. Ex : We must adapt to a changing world.

questions.question: assimilate sth
questions.verso: assimiler — learn and get used to sth which is new and different. Ex : It takes time to assimilate new ideas. Nom : assimilation.

questions.question: What does « assimilate sth » mean?
choix: change back to a state or situation that existed in the past (syn. go back)
change gradually, often from something simple to something more complicated
change sth so it is the opposite of what it was before (reverse a decision/trend/policy)
learn and get used to sth which is new and different
questions.explication: assimilate sth = assimiler. Ex : It takes time to assimilate new ideas.

questions.question: evolve
questions.verso: évoluer — change gradually, often from something simple to something more complicated. Ex : Democracy has evolved over hundreds of years. Nom : evolution.

questions.question: What does « evolve » mean?
choix: improve a system, an organization, a law by making changes to it
learn and get used to sth which is new and different
make changes to correct a mistake or improve a law, statement, document
change gradually, often from something simple to something more complicated
questions.explication: evolve = évoluer. Ex : Democracy has evolved over hundreds of years.

questions.question: transition
questions.verso: une transition — a process or period of change from one state to another. Ex : We hope for a smooth transition. Nom : transition (in transition).

questions.question: What does « transition » mean?
choix: a process or period of change from one state to another
change sth so it is the opposite of what it was before (reverse a decision/trend/policy)
change your behaviour in order to be more successful in a new situation (syn. adjust to)
completely change the appearance or character of sth, often to make it better
questions.explication: transition = une transition. Ex : We hope for a smooth transition.

questions.question: revert (back) to sth
questions.verso: revenir à — change back to a state or situation that existed in the past (syn. go back). Ex : After weeks of unrest, life has reverted to normal. Nom : reversion.

questions.question: What does « revert (back) to sth » mean?
choix: a process or period of change from one state to another
improve a system, an organization, a law by making changes to it
make changes to correct a mistake or improve a law, statement, document
change back to a state or situation that existed in the past (syn. go back)
questions.explication: revert (back) to sth = revenir à. Ex : After weeks of unrest, life has reverted to normal.

questions.question: restore sth
questions.verso: restaurer, rétablir — return sth to its former state or condition. Ex : Some people want to restore the monarchy. Nom : restoration.

questions.question: What does « restore sth » mean?
choix: improve a system, an organization, a law by making changes to it
a process or period of change from one state to another
return sth to its former state or condition
learn and get used to sth which is new and different
questions.explication: restore sth = restaurer, rétablir. Ex : Some people want to restore the monarchy.

questions.question: reverse sth
questions.verso: inverser, revenir sur — change sth so it is the opposite of what it was before (reverse a decision/trend/policy). Ex : They reversed their decision. Nom : reversal (adj. reversible ≠ irreversible).

questions.question: What does « reverse sth » mean?
choix: change sth so it is the opposite of what it was before (reverse a decision/trend/policy)
learn and get used to sth which is new and different
change back to a state or situation that existed in the past (syn. go back)
completely change the appearance or character of sth, often to make it better
questions.explication: reverse sth = inverser, revenir sur. Ex : They reversed their decision.

questions.question: reform sth
questions.verso: réformer — improve a system, an organization, a law by making changes to it. Ex : There are new proposals to reform the prison system. Nom : reform.

questions.question: What does « reform sth » mean?
choix: change back to a state or situation that existed in the past (syn. go back)
change gradually, often from something simple to something more complicated
improve a system, an organization, a law by making changes to it
change sth so it is the opposite of what it was before (reverse a decision/trend/policy)
questions.explication: reform sth = réformer. Ex : There are new proposals to reform the prison system.

questions.question: There will be a period of ___ when the new government takes over.
The building was badly damaged, but they are planning to ___ it.
As a company we believe in ___, not revolution.
They've changed their minds completely: this is a ___ of the previous policy.
After years of civil war, the country will find it difficult to ___ back to normal.
If only climate change could be ___ to leave a better planet to our children!
We will all have to ___ to climate change, or it will be a disaster for the planet.
Once the ice caps melt at the poles, the change is completely ___.
We'll need time to ___ all the new ideas in their proposed plan.
The Security Council urgently needs to be ___. (réformer, participe passé)
The General Assembly voted to ___ the resolution to correct a mistake. (amender)
Which word describes a COMPLETE change?
choix: transform
amend
revert
evolve

questions.question: Which words describe a GRADUAL change? (plusieurs réponses)
choix: transition
reverse
transform
evolve
revert
questions.explication: evolve (évoluer progressivement) et transition (période de changement).

questions.question: Which words describe changing BACK to a previous state? (plusieurs réponses)
choix: restore
assimilate
transform
evolve
revert

questions.question: What is the opposite of « reversible »?
choix: irreversible
unreversible
non-reverse
disreversible

questions.question: Match the nouns: which are correct? (plusieurs réponses)
choix: restore → restoration
amend → amendment
evolve → evolution
restore → restorement
reverse → reversement
amend → amendation
reverse → reversal
questions.explication: amendment, restoration, evolution, reversal, transformation, assimilation, reform.
